function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑use set of files** that you can drop into the `nodejs-welcome` repository, followed by a short “cheat‑sheet” of the commands you’ll run locally to finish the job.

> **TL;DR**  
> 1. Clone the repo.  
> 2. Add the three new files (`Dockerfile`, `k8s/deployment.yaml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).  
> 3. Commit & push.  

---

## 1️⃣  Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> If you don’t have SSH keys set up, use HTTPS instead:
> `git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`

---

## 2️⃣  Analyse the repo

A quick look at the repo shows:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `package.json` | Node.js dependencies & scripts |
| `app.js` (or similar) | Main entry point |
| `README.md` | Project description |
| `Dockerfile` (missing) | Container build |
| `k8s/` (missing) | Deployment manifests |
| `.github/workflows/` (missing) | CI/CD pipelines |

The app is a standard Express/Node.js service that listens on **port 3000** (check `app.listen(3000)` or the `PORT` env var).

---

## 3️⃣  Create the Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the repo root:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Install build dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["npm", "start"]
```

> *Why this Dockerfile?*  
> * `node:18-alpine` is small, fast, and contains the latest LTS Node.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a reproducible install.  
> * The container listens on port 3000 – the same port the app uses locally.

---

## 4️⃣  Create Kubernetes manifests

Create a directory `k8s/` and inside it a file `deployment.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
  labels:
    app: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nodejs-welcome
          image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change if you use another registry
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
          env:
            - name: NODE_ENV
              value: production
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 3000
```

> *What this does:*  
> * Deploys 2 replicas of the container.  
> * Exposes the app via a `ClusterIP` service on port 80 (internally forwarded to 3000).  
> * Uses the image that will be built by the GitHub Actions workflow.

---

## 5️⃣  Create a GitHub Actions workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` and add a file `ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI / Build & Push

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '18'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test || true   # change if you have real tests

      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build -t ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker tag ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **Important notes**  
> * The workflow uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` to authenticate to `ghcr.io`.  
> * If you prefer Docker Hub or another registry, replace the registry URL and credentials accordingly.  
> * The `npm test` step is optional – if you don’t have tests, you can remove it or replace it with a lint step.

---

## 6️⃣  Add, commit, and push

```bash
# Stage the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"

# Push to main
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run, build the Docker image, and push it to GitHub Container Registry.  
> You can then deploy the app to any Kubernetes cluster by applying the manifest:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

---

## 🎉  Done!

You now have:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deploys the app to Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image |

Feel free to tweak the image tags, registry, or deployment settings to match your environment. Happy coding!
